curated.question: How many drawings failed compliance review this week, out of how many reviewed?
curated.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT drawing_id) AS drawings_reviewed,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN status = 'FAIL' THEN drawing_id END) AS drawings_failed,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN status = 'PASS' THEN drawing_id END) AS drawings_passed
FROM mfg_mc_se_sa.bluerridge_gold_pm.compliance_findings
WHERE review_date BETWEEN '2026-10-31' AND '2026-11-06'
curated.expected_answer: 51 of 238 drawings failed this week (187 passed).

curated.question: Show failed compliance findings this week by code citation.
curated.sql:
SELECT citation, COUNT(*) AS failed_findings, COUNT(DISTINCT drawing_id) AS drawings
FROM mfg_mc_se_sa.bluerridge_gold_pm.compliance_findings
WHERE status = 'FAIL' AND review_date BETWEEN '2026-10-31' AND '2026-11-06'
GROUP BY citation
ORDER BY failed_findings DESC
curated.expected_answer: Failed findings by citation: ASME B31.3 §322: 30; OSHA 1910.147: 25; ASME B16.5 §4.2: 15; IBC 1005.1: 8; ASME B31.3 §341: 7.

rule.desc: the five citations and their finding counts (30, 25, 15, 8, 7) all appear

curated.question: Which milestones are already late, and by how many days?
curated.sql:
SELECT milestone_id, name, discipline, planned_end, days_late
FROM mfg_mc_se_sa.bluerridge_gold_pm.schedule_overdue
WHERE days_late > 0
ORDER BY days_late DESC
curated.expected_answer: 6 milestones are late: MS-271 15 days; MS-277 11 days; MS-278 5 days; MS-281 4 days; MS-279 4 days; MS-287 2 days. MS-274 is due today (0 days late) and is not late.

rule.desc: ID+days equality for the 6 late milestones; MS-274 (due today) must not be in the result rows

curated.question: What are the top 3 highest-risk milestones in the next 90 days?

curated.question: What does OSHA 1910.147 require?
curated.sql:
SELECT citation_label, title, text
FROM mfg_mc_se_sa.bluerridge_agents.code_excerpts
WHERE citation_label = 'OSHA 1910.147'

expected_rows.text: Control of hazardous energy: lockout and tagout. Before anyone services or maintains a machine or piece of equipment, the equipment must be isolated from all sources of hazardous energy and locked or tagged out so that it cannot start up or release stored energy. Each machine needs identified energy isolation points, such as breakers, valves and disconnects, where a lock or tag can be applied. A reviewer checks the drawing for lockout and tagout isolation points, tags or notes on each piece of equipment, and flags equipment that shows no lockout or isolation provision.
expected_rows.title: Control of hazardous energy: lockout and tagout

curated.expected_answer: Clause titled 'Control of hazardous energy: lockout and tagout': the paraphrased text says equipment must be isolated from hazardous energy and locked/tagged out before servicing (lockout/tagout).

rule.desc: answer contains the clause title 'Control of hazardous energy' and 'lockout', and the SQL reads code_excerpts

curated.question: How accurate is the AI compliance judge?
curated.sql:
SELECT prompt_version, eval_column, ROUND(`precision` * 100, 1) AS precision_pct, ROUND(recall * 100, 1) AS recall_pct
FROM mfg_mc_se_sa.bluerridge_gold_pm.compliance_eval
WHERE prompt_version = 'v3_final' AND eval_column = 'C' AND citation = 'ALL'
curated.expected_answer: The v3 judge (column C, all citations) has precision 58.1% and recall 81.0%.

rule.desc: precision 58.1% and recall 81.0% (a 0-1 fraction is accepted as the same value)
